question: What is the name of the festival celebrated simultaneously by unmarried tribal girls during the Karam celebrations in Jharkhand and eastern India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jawa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Jawa** is a festival celebrated during the Karam festivities in Jharkhand and eastern India, primarily by unmarried tribal girls.
 
• The celebration involves the worship of germinated grains, symbolizing fertility, prosperity, and the life cycle.
 
• This festival is deeply rooted in tribal culture and traditions, where young girls pray for the well-being of their families and good fortune.
 
• Jawa is an integral part of Karam Puja, which marks the beginning of agricultural activities and honors nature.
 
• It showcases the rich cultural heritage of tribal communities and their connection to nature and agriculture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sohrai:**

 
 
• Sohrai is a harvest festival celebrated by tribal communities in Jharkhand, Bihar, and West Bengal.
 
• It is associated with cattle worship and the decoration of mud walls with traditional tribal art.
 
• The festival is marked by feasting, dancing, and rituals to thank nature for the harvest.
 
 
 
• **Karma:**
 
 
• Karma is a popular tribal festival in Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and Madhya Pradesh.
 
• The festival centers around the worship of the Karam tree, which is considered sacred and symbolizes fertility and prosperity.
 
• During Karma, people sing and dance around the Karam tree to celebrate nature and the agricultural cycle.
 
 
 
• **Madai:**
 
 
• Madai is a tribal festival celebrated in the state of Chhattisgarh.
 
• It is a fair-like event featuring cultural performances, rituals, and offerings to deities.
 
• The festival is an important occasion for social gatherings and the display of tribal art, dance, and music.
